questions.question: What was the last day of the year 1961?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Given: January 1, 1961 was Sunday.

1961 was an ordinary year.

Since, an ordinary year has 365 days:

365 ÷ 7 = 52 weeks and 1 odd day

So, the last day shifts by 1 day from Sunday.

Therefore, December 31, 1961 was Sunday.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4".**

questions.question: Runs scored by 5 boys R, B, C, L and Q are compared. Runs of no two boys are same. Runs of B are less than Q but more than C. Runs of L are more than R but less than C. How many boys scored runs more than L?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Given:

Runs of B are less than Q but more than C.

So, the order is: Q > B > C

Runs of L are more than R but less than C.

So, C > L > R

Combining both conditions: Q > B > C > L > R

F is the immediate neighbour of A, but is not to the immediate left of A. G is not the immediate neighbour of F or C. E is the immediate neighbour of A and D. questions.solution:

Given: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre.

questions.question:
Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8046710e4a703f8072aa91b9d679fb7913c05aea002bd44883a897821eb5a2bd.png]
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: The elements from the first figure shift their structural positions to form the second figure by cycling through a specific layout pattern.

The first pair:

The first element of the bottom row moves to the first position of the top row.

The remaining elements of the top row shift one position to the right.

The last element of the top row moves to the last position of the bottom row.

The remaining elements of the bottom row shift one position to the left.

The second pair:

The first element of the bottom row (Circle) moves to the first position of the top row.

The remaining elements of the top row (S, T, Triangle) shift one position to the right.

The last element of the top row (P) moves to the last position of the bottom row.

The remaining elements of the bottom row (L, K, Square) shift one position to the left.

This gives the final arrangement as:

Top Row → Circle, S, T, Triangle

Bottom Row → L, K, Square, P

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ed83a29b3be30491b32050231f2ed6be4af1800734e1b06b8e724a774d27b2b6.png] 

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

questions.question: In a certain code language, 'HEIGHT' is coded as '103' and 'ALLOW' is coded as '70'. How will 'FAME' be coded in that code language?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2ef66797889264a1e003c29556be62ec8bd30e7989c90048a8bac955e67b6d42.png] 

The logic followed here is:

Logic: Code = Sum of the positional values of the letters in the alphabet.

Given: HEIGHT →

H(8) + E(5) + I(9) + G(7) + H(8) + T(20) = 57

Since, the code is 103:

57 + 46 = 103

For, ALLOW →

A(1) + L(12) + L(12) + O(15) + W(23) = 63

63 + 7 = 70

Checking simple direct relation from options:

FAME →

F(6) + A(1) + M(13) + E(5) = 25

25 × 3 + 4 = 79

So, FAME → 79

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 4.**
